findings.passage: “Voters have voiced their concerns loud and clear, and yet, the governor repeatedly said that he will veto legislation to increase the validity of the Commonwealth’s election process. Unfortunately, he still seems to be ruling without consideration of the majority of state residents, much like how he handled the pandemic for a year,” Sen. Stefano said. “It’s disappointing, but we can’t let that stop us from being responsive to Pennsylvanians’ needs.”
findings.note: Quote in his office's press release on Senate passage of SB 735, a proposed constitutional amendment asking voters whether ID should be required each time a ballot is cast. He criticises the governor's stated veto of election-process legislation. The release says he supported the measure. The original page is gone (404), so the archived copy is cited.

findings.passage: The Senate today approved a plan to allow voters to decide if the Pennsylvania Constitution should be amended to require identification each time a voter casts a ballot, according to Sen. Pat Stefano (R-32), who supported the measure.
findings.note: Opening line of the same press release from his office. It is the office's description, not a direct quote of him, and says he supported SB 735.

findings.passage: The COVID-19 pandemic changed the way we handle voting in Pennsylvania, and our social media platforms amplify any issues that arise. Clear communication and minor fixes to the election code will alleviate most of the concerns.
findings.note: His written answer in the WESA candidate survey, to a question about discontent with the two major political parties. He mentions voting rules only briefly. No mention of ID or citizenship.
